-------Respondents For Petitioner : Ms. Priyanka Rai, Advocate For Respondents-State : Mr. Swajeet S. Ubeja, Panel Lawyer For Respondent No. 5 : Mr. Sanjay Patel, Advocate SB:Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu,
Judge ORDER ON BOARD 14/06/2024 1.

Petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking following reliefs:-
"10.1 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call the entire records pertaining to the case of the petitioner.
10.2

That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the Respondent authorities not to interfere in the land of the petitioner without any authority or in alternative the Respondent authorities may be directed to pay adequate compensation as per the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 10.3

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Any appropriate writ, direction or order may also kindly be passed in favour of the petitioner, which this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the circumstances of the case"

2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner is in possession of land bearing khasra No.
1227/1 measuring 0.400 Hect. out of 0.9800 Hect. situated at village Kohka, P.H. No. 45 Tahsil and District Durg.
Petitioner came in possession of the said land by way of registered gift deed executed in her favour.

Petitioner is still in possession of the land, however, Respondent No. 5 is making an Smt. Charanjeet Kour vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74870060/
1 attempt to encroach upon the land possessed by her and therefore writ petition is filed.

sentences.text:
She also pointed out that on the application submitted by petitioner, the revenue officers have demarcated the land on spot, copy of demarcation report is placed on record as Annexure P-4 and therefore Respondent No. 5 be restrain from interfering with peaceful possession of petitioner.
3. Learned counsel for Respondent No. 5 opposes the submission and raises an objection with regard to maintainability of the writ petition in view of the nature of relief claimed.
He submits that the relief claimed by the petitioner is in way of seeking injunction from this Court restraining respondent No. 5 from interfering the possession.
Petitioner is having efficacious remedy under the law for seeking injunction by way of filing appropriate proceeding before the civil court.

He also contended that the demarcation report relied upon by the petitioner does not specifically mention that the respondent No. 5 or any other person is in encroachment over the land owned by petitioner.
If her submission is to be accepted, the petition is bereft of merit and no relief can be granted.
4. Learned State counsel submits that the grievance of the petitioner is against respondent No. 5 and therefore he is not making submission on merit.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the documents placed on record.

6. From perusal of the relief No. 10.2 would show that the petitioner has sought a relief of direction to be issued to respondents not to interfere with the peaceful possession with the property of the petitioner.
The demarcation report which is relied upon by the petitioner dated 14.08.2023 does not specifically mention of any of the person has encroached upon any portion of the land owned by petitioner.

Even if there is demarcation report in favour of petitioner, the petitioner could have filed appropriate proceeding before the appropriate forum seeking injunction against any of the respondent from interference with the peaceful possession of the petitioner.
7. For the foregoing discussion, I am not inclined to entertain this writ petition, it is accordingly dismissed.
However, petitioner would be at liberty to approach appropriate forum by filing appropriate proceeding for redressal of her grievance, if so advised.

Sd/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) Judge /pawan
